title: Canonical closed-test section and representative maps
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with coefficients $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ on the small pro-etale sites [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use their exact inverse images $g^*$, direct images $g_*$ and unbounded derived functors [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], localization $Q$ of complexes [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the universal right-derived units [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For a test $W\to Y$, define $\operatorname{evaluation}_W(F)=F(W)$ on the underlying abelian sheaf. For an additive functor $F$, define $\operatorname{complexes}(F)$ by applying $F$ termwise to unbounded cochain complexes. Define $\operatorname{pushEvaluation}_{g,W}:\operatorname{evaluation}_W g_*\cong\operatorname{evaluation}_{Y'\times_Y W}$ by the literal direct-image section formula, and $\operatorname{evaluationMap}_b:F(W)\to F(W')$ by restriction along a test arrow $b:W'\to W$.
For a commutative ring $A$ and an ideal $I$, define $\operatorname{closedMap}:\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ by the quotient homomorphism [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For an affine ind-etale test $V$ over $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, define $\operatorname{liftedTest}(V)=v(V)$ using the closed-site lift and its canonical inclusion $i_V:V\to v(V)$ [def-exc-closed-site-lift], and $\operatorname{closedTest}(V)=V$, both regarded in the full small sites. Define $\operatorname{testFibre}(f,W)=W\times_Y X$ over $X$ for $f:X\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $\operatorname{closedUnit}:F(v(V))\to(s^*F)(V)$ by the actual $s^*\dashv s_*$ unit, the direct-image section formula, and restriction along the canonical closed-fibre arrow. The unit-section convention is [def-sfb-proetale-inverse-image-unit-section].
For a cartesian square $(h:X_Z\to X,f_Z:X_Z\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I),f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A,s)$, define $\operatorname{testArrow}:T_0\to T$, where $T=\operatorname{testFibre}(f,v(V))$ and $T_0=\operatorname{testFibre}(f_Z,V)$, by the pullback projections and $i_V,h$. Define $\operatorname{testPullbackComposition}:h^*(-)|_{T_0}\cong a^*((-)|_T)$ from the specified inverse-image compositors and the equality of the two maps $T_0\to X$, with $a=\operatorname{testArrow}$. Define $\operatorname{derivedTestPullbackComposition}$ by descending this particular comparison with the exact-functor localization factors. Localized coefficients and sections use the restricted ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].
For any complex $L$ and isomorphism $e:Q(L)\cong K$, define $\operatorname{pushModel}_{f,K,L,e}:Q(f_*L)\to Rf_*K$ by the universal right-derived unit at $L$ followed by $Rf_*(e)$. For a quasi-isomorphism $j:h^*L\to J$, define $\operatorname{pullRepresentative}:Q(J)\cong h^*K$ as $(Qj)^{-1}$ followed by the exact-pullback localization factor and $h^*(e)$. Define $\operatorname{localizationModel}_{W,K,L,e}:Q(L(W))\to R\Gamma(W,K|_W)$ by the universal derived-evaluation unit, the derived map of the actual localization unit-section map, and the image of $e$. The localization unit-section map is the actual $W^*\dashv W_*$ unit followed by the direct-image section formula and restriction along the diagonal $W\to W\times_YW$. These are constructions of maps and canonical composition isomorphisms, with no assertion that $\operatorname{closedUnit}$, $\operatorname{pushModel}$ or $\operatorname{localizationModel}$ is invertible; no affineness or weak-contractibility hypothesis is imposed beyond the affine closed-lift input.
